Deliverables: the NativeScheduler source/build only where a confirmed regression requires repair, a fresh Debug app build, and observable evidence under .omo/evidence/functional-recovery. Success criteria: (1) establish a source-and-history-backed feature inventory and reproduce why the previously launched build looked design-only; (2) through computer-use on the real app, prove Tasks add/edit/complete/reorder/persistence behavior and empty-state controls; (3) through computer-use on the real app, prove Timer mode/category/start/pause/resume/stop behavior plus Dayline live detail and expand/collapse behavior; (4) through computer-use on the real app, prove shell Settings opens and category/settings interactions remain available; (5) Swift diagnostics, targeted tests, app build, and a final fresh launch are clean, with every criterion evidenced by non-empty screenshots/action logs. Scope bounds: preserve the current visual design and proportions; do not redesign, delete user data, modify unrelated functionality, use destructive git commands, or create commits without explicit user authorization. If source already contains a function but the wrong/stale/test-isolated executable caused the symptom, fix the launch path rather than rewriting the feature. I will stop right away when all inventoried existing functions pass their real-app scenarios in the latest design build and that verified app is left running for the user.

successCriteria.scenario: Auxiliary CLI/source scenario: capture running PID executable path and hashes; enumerate every current user control and its action/persistence wiring from source/tests; compare SwiftPM and Xcode products; reproduce the design-only report against the running app AX tree and isolated/user data state. PASS only when one evidence-backed root cause is confirmed or the symptom is precisely reclassified with all competing launch hypotheses refuted.
successCriteria.expectedEvidence: Non-empty .omo/evidence/ulw/native-scheduler-functional-recovery-20260817/G001-outcome-the-current-nativescheduler/a1/C001/inventory.json plus baseline-ax.txt and baseline.png in the same C001 directory, containing file:line implementation references, PID executable path, artifact hashes, data-state observation, and confirmed/refuted hypotheses.

successCriteria.scenario: Computer-use happy-path scenario on an isolated real Debug app: expand shell; create/rename/reorder/complete/reopen/delete a folder and task; switch timer mode, adjust duration/end time, add/select category, start/pause/resume/stop; inspect live Dayline detail and toggle compact/expanded; capture every state transition. PASS only if every inventoried Tasks/Timer/Dayline action changes visible or persisted state exactly once without changing the approved design.
successCriteria.expectedEvidence: Non-empty C002/action-log.txt, ordered Tasks/Timer/Dayline screenshots, and persistence-dump.txt under .omo/evidence/ulw/native-scheduler-functional-recovery-20260817/G001-outcome-the-current-nativescheduler/a1; cleanup receipt proves isolated QA process/home stopped and removed.

successCriteria.scenario: Computer-use regression/adversarial scenario: from empty isolated state open shell Settings, verify close, launch-at-login/default duration/default mode controls and category add/edit/delete confirmation without altering the user profile; relaunch to verify persisted safe settings/category state; run Swift diagnostics, focused tests, full package tests, and fresh Xcode Debug build; launch the verified user-profile app and confirm the current balanced design and all controls remain available. PASS only if all change-caused checks are clean and any unrelated pre-existing failure is independently reproduced and documented.
successCriteria.expectedEvidence: Non-empty .omo/evidence/functional-recovery/C003/settings-action-log.txt, settings/relaunch/final-app screenshots, diagnostics.txt, focused-tests.txt, full-tests.txt, xcode-build.txt, binary provenance.txt, and cleanup receipt; final verified app PID remains running for user after evidence is recorded.
